For those just tuning in or new to OSINT (Open Source Intelligence) on X, welcome to the world of raw intelligence. There are a large number of accounts out there advertising themselves as OSINT providers.  
Military intelligence is comprised of many fields, OSINT is merely one of them, but has emerged as a leader among the general population because military intelligence work products themselves are most often classified to protect sources and methods.  OSINT has gained in popularity because it offers the public a glimpse into the otherwise secretive world of military intelligence.  

By discipline the field military intelligence itself is broken down into many fields, of which, OSINT is merely one segment:

**Human Intelligence (HUMINT): Gathers and analyzes information from human sources, such as informants, defectors, or interrogations. Focuses on motives, intentions, and relationships.

**Signals Intelligence (SIGINT): Collects and examines intercepted communications, electronic signals, or telemetry. Includes subcategories like:

**Communications Intelligence (COMINT): Gathers and analyzes intercepted messages (e.g., phone calls, emails).

**Electronic Intelligence (ELINT): Collects and analyzes of non-communication signals (e.g., radar, missile telemetry).

**Geospatial Intelligence (GEOINT): Collects and interprets imagery, maps, and spatial data from satellites, drones, or other sensors to assess locations, infrastructure, or activities.

**Measurement and Signature Intelligence (MASINT): Collects and analyzes technical data, such as chemical, biological, or electromagnetic signatures, to detect weapons, materials, or environmental changes.

**Open-Source Intelligence (OSINT): Collects and evaluates publicly available information from media, social media, academic papers, or websites (e.g., analyzing X posts for sentiment or trends).

**Financial Intelligence (FININT) Analysis: Collects and tracks financial transactions to uncover money laundering, terrorism funding, or illicit networks.

**Cyber Intelligence (CI): Focuses on identifying and analyzing cyber threats, hacking activities, or digital infrastructure vulnerabilities, often combining SIGINT and OSINT.

Once gathered or collected, the field of military intelligence then participates in the analysis of that information and is generally broken down by Analytical Focus into the following categories: 

Strategic Intelligence Analysis: Assesses long-term trends, threats, or opportunities at a national or global level (e.g., geopolitical shifts, economic forecasts).

Operational Intelligence Analysis: Supports mid-term planning and execution, such as military campaigns or law enforcement operations.

Tactical Intelligence Analysis: Provides immediate, actionable insights for specific missions or activities (e.g., battlefield movements, criminal arrests).

Counterintelligence Analysis: Identifies and neutralizes foreign intelligence operations, espionage, or insider threats.

Competitive Intelligence Analysis: Used in business to analyze competitors’ strategies, market trends, or consumer behavior.

Threat Intelligence Analysis: Focuses on identifying and mitigating specific threats, such as terrorism, cyberattacks, or organized crime.

Political Intelligence Analysis: Evaluates political dynamics, leadership intentions, or policy changes in a country or region.

Economic Intelligence Analysis: Analyzes economic indicators, trade policies, or market conditions to predict impacts on security or business.

OSINT itself is of course not limited to X, though I believe X offers the most information to the general public.  Providers here contribute information from many segments of the intelligence field. 

Not all OSINT sites are equal and not all are credible or reliable. It's important to consider that many OSINT accounts come from all over the world, so their focus and underlying interests will vary greatly, as will their analyses as well as the quality of them.  I would urge followers to spend some time determining if the OSINT accounts they are following may be putting out misleading or false information. Many accounts are affiliated with or operated by foreign governments although they may not appear to be. Exercising caution when evaluating the information you're receiving is important.  Information is used as a weapon to influence- so you'll often see OSINT accounts blatantly telling outright lies or engaged in deception operations that are meant to influence public opinion and they are often successful. 

How do you determine when an OSINT account is credible and reliable? Generally speaking, my rule of thumb is to look at who follows them.  When you see known and credible OSINT providers following each other it tends to be because we find those accounts to be credible and reliable sources of information ourselves.  When you see accredited media and new organizations, world leaders, diplomats, embassies, or government officials (past or present) or other government agencies, published authors, academics and journalists openly following an OSINT account, that is a good indicator you're following a credible account.  

I know and take a lot of pride in the fact that my account is followed by a number of these people or organizations related to my niche field in the Indo-Pacific.  I try to source information from credible sources- and most often repost information from OSINT accounts that I trust.  Of course, our field is prone to mistakes- but I know for me, and for those OSINT accounts that I follow, great efforts are made to ensure that we're posting accurate information because very often the information that we *do* post can and does contribute to and influence decisions made by governments around the world. You won't see non-credible OSINT sources followed by any of these people- particularly by diplomats and government officials. 

We are aggregators of information and while most of us are often very highly opinionated, credible OSINT accounts are NOT "content creators" attempting to influence public opinion. When we have an opinion, you can generally discern that it's a personal opinion versus raw intelligence. 

So as conflicts rage around the world, OSINT is very helpful in providing raw information that very often makes its way into main stream media- so you tend to see things naked and in the raw here before it ends up on Fox News, CNN or Sky News or the New York Times- or news wire services like Reuters and the Associated Press.  

Personally, I find it both humbling and flattering that everyone who chooses to follow me does so, and I certainly feel a sense of moral and ethical responsibility to ensure that the information aggregation that post and repost is as accurate as it can be.  I don't believe I'd have as many influential followers from among the many I mentioned above were not that the case. 

With, I want to say thank you to everyone who chooses to follow me. I don't make any money doing this and have no plans to do that.  I am fortunate that I'm able to have the time to do this and in many ways, it can feel like a full time job, but one of the reasons I enjoy it so much is because the knowledge I gain here itself has a lot of value in helping me try to understand the world in which we live. It's a crazy place at times as I'm sure you'll agree. I also very much enjoy the friendships I've made along the way- that in a lot of cases are friendships in real life also.  The folks I've met are simply amazing people in their own right. I suppose in many ways, that makes a lot of OSINT providers HUMINT assets- but in truth, we're all assets to our families and loved ones, friends and partners around the world as well a people who want help make the world an informed and better place to live.  

So again, many thanks to all of you for following! My DMs are open. If I don't get back to you right away, please don't take it personally.  I am frequently inundated with messages but I try to respond to everyone although I won't lie- my priority tends to be those with whom I interact regularly here or who serve as sources for the information I post or repost.  I also have a life that's international both in the USA and Philippines, so my schedule can be crazy with family issues and raising kids.  Yes, Frankie is a pseudonym. While it's certainly possible to find out my real identity, I have, in the past, received credible death threats against me and my family so I choose anonymity here for the sake of safety. I don't find that being unreasonable and suspect none of you do either. 

Keep up the fire and stay safe! 🇺🇸🇵🇭 -Frankie

Kahit gaano kabilis o katagal ang pagparada, malaki ang epekto sa daloy ng trapiko. 

Nagpapatupad ang iba't ibang traffic enforcement districts ng Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) ng clearing operations para sa mas maluwag na daloy ng trapiko.

Ang bawat operasyon sa Mabuhay Lanes at mga pangunahing kalsada sa Kalakhang Maynila ay para maging passable at obstruction-free ang mga kalsada at bangketa.

Para sa sagabal sa mga secondary roads at mas maliliit pang daan sa Metro Manila, makipag-ugnayan sa lokal na pamahalaan na sumasakop sa lugar para mag-report.
#mmda
